extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies, agency heads, and regulatory policy officials (e.g., OMB/OIRA staff) responsible for rulemaking and regulatory review
extracted.subtask_description: Executive Order establishing principles and requirements for how federal agencies should design, analyze, adopt, and review regulations — including public participation, cost–benefit analysis, science integrity, flexible approaches, retrospective review, and interagency coordination. Intended to guide agency rulemaking and regulatory review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory system dual objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Our regulatory system must protect public health, welfare, safety, and our environment while promoting economic growth, innovation, competitiveness, and job creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement frames regulation as requiring balanced consideration of protective goals and pro-growth goals; subsequent provisions explain how to operationalize this balance (science, costs/benefits, least burdensome tools, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of best available science
rubrics_metrics.description: It must be based on the best available science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure objectivity of scientific and technological information and processes used to support regulatory actions (see Sec. 5; consistent with the Presidential Memorandum on Scientific Integrity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation and open exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: It must allow for public participation and an open exchange of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are directed to provide meaningful opportunities for public comment and to seek views of affected stakeholders, state/local/tribal officials, and experts (see Sec. 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote predictability and reduce uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: It must promote predictability and reduce uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design should favor approaches that increase regulatory clarity and reduce compliance uncertainty for regulated parties and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use best, innovative, least-burdensome tools
rubrics_metrics.description: It must identify and use the best, most innovative, and least burdensome tools for achieving regulatory ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider a range of tools and favor those that achieve objectives with minimal unnecessary burden; see also Sec. 4 on flexible approaches and Sec. 1(b)(5) on alternatives to direct regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider benefits and costs (quantitative and qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: It must take into account benefits and costs, both quantitative and qualitative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should quantify where possible and discuss qualitatively values that are difficult to quantify (e.g., equity, human dignity, fairness, distributive impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible, consistent, plain-language regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: It must ensure that regulations are accessible, consistent, written in plain language, and easy to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text and supporting materials should be drafted for clarity and accessibility to facilitate compliance and public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and improve actual results
rubrics_metrics.description: It must measure, and seek to improve, the actual results of regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should monitor the real-world outcomes of regulations and use evidence to make rules more effective and less burdensome (ties to retrospective review in Sec. 6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoned determination that benefits justify costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose or adopt a regulation only upon a reasoned determination that its benefits justify its costs (recognizing that some benefits and costs are difficult to quantify).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must document a reasoned analysis showing that benefits outweigh costs when choosing to regulate; qualitative benefits/costs should be acknowledged where quantification is infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor regulations to impose least burden consistent with objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Tailor regulations to impose the least burden on society, consistent with obtaining regulatory objectives, taking into account, among other things, and to the extent practicable, the costs of cumulative regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design should consider distribution of burdens, cumulative impacts of multiple rules, and seek less onerous alternatives that still achieve objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select approaches that maximize net benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Select, in choosing among alternative regulatory approaches, those approaches that maximize net benefits (including potential economic, environmental, public health and safety, and other advantages; distributive impacts; and equity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisionmaking should compare alternatives on net-benefit grounds and explicitly consider distributional and equity effects as part of the net calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify performance objectives where feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent feasible, specify performance objectives, rather than specifying the behavior or manner of compliance that regulated entities must adopt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor outcome- or performance-based standards over prescriptive rules so regulated parties have flexibility in how to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and assess alternatives to direct regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and assess available alternatives to direct regulation, including providing economic incentives to encourage the desired behavior, such as user fees or marketable permits, or providing information upon which choices can be made by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider non-coercive instruments (incentives, information, market mechanisms) as possible substitutes or complements to command-and-control regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use best available techniques to quantify benefits and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the best available techniques to quantify anticipated present and future benefits and costs as accurately as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply state-of-the-art analytic methods, transparently document assumptions, and update methods as improved techniques become available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider qualitative values difficult to quantify
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate and permitted by law, each agency may consider (and discuss qualitatively) values that are difficult or impossible to quantify, including equity, human dignity, fairness, and distributive impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When monetary valuation is infeasible, agencies should explicitly describe and weigh qualitative societal values in the regulatory analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation process and stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations shall be adopted through a process that involves public participation; based, to the extent feasible and consistent with law, on the open exchange of information and perspectives among State, local, and tribal officials, experts in relevant disciplines, affected stakeholders in the private sector, and the public as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage a broad cross-section of affected parties and experts during rule development to inform regulatory choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period and online docket access
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall afford the public a meaningful opportunity to comment through the Internet on any proposed regulation, with a comment period that should generally be at least 60 days.  For proposed and final rules, provide timely online access to the rulemaking docket on regulations.gov, including relevant scientific and technical findings, in an open format that can be easily searched and downloaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer comment periods and full, searchable online dockets (including scientific and technical material) are encouraged to enable informed public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for public comment on all pertinent docket parts
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed rules, such access shall include, to the extent feasible and permitted by law, an opportunity for public comment on all pertinent parts of the rulemaking docket, including relevant scientific and technical findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should allow comments on the full evidentiary record supporting a proposal, not just the proposed regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek views of likely affected parties before NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking, each agency, where feasible and appropriate, shall seek the views of those who are likely to be affected, including those who are likely to benefit from and those who are potentially subject to such rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early outreach to both beneficiaries and regulated entities helps identify issues and reduce unintended burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination, simplification, and harmonization across agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall attempt to promote coordination, simplification, and harmonization across agencies to reduce redundant, inconsistent, or overlapping regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interagency coordination can reduce compliance costs and confusion caused by fragmented or conflicting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote regulatory approaches that foster innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall also seek to identify, as appropriate, means to achieve regulatory goals that are designed to promote innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing rules, consider approaches that encourage technological and process innovation rather than impede it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider flexible approaches to reduce burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: Where relevant, feasible, and consistent with regulatory objectives, each agency shall identify and consider regulatory approaches that reduce burdens and maintain flexibility and freedom of choice for the public.  These approaches include warnings, appropriate default rules, and disclosure requirements as well as provision of information to the public in a form that is clear and intelligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lighter-touch tools (warnings, defaults, disclosures, information provision) where they can achieve objectives with less intrusion on liberty and business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific integrity and objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall ensure the objectivity of any scientific and technological information and processes used to support the agency's regulatory actions (consistent with the President's Memorandum 'Scientific Integrity').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain safeguards and policies to protect scientific integrity in research, analysis, and decisionmaking that underpins regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective analysis and periodic review of significant regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall consider how best to promote retrospective analysis of rules that may be outmoded, ineffective, insufficient, or excessively burdensome, and to modify, streamline, expand, or repeal them in accordance with what has been learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retrospective analyses should be evidence-based, include supporting data, and be released online whenever possible to inform reform of existing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit preliminary plan for periodic review to OIRA within 120 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 120 days of the date of this order, each agency shall develop and submit to the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs a preliminary plan, consistent with law and its resources and regulatory priorities, under which the agency will periodically review its existing significant regulations to determine whether any such regulations should be modified, streamlined, expanded, or repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must timely document how they will carry out ongoing retrospective review of significant regulations and set priorities consistent with available resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation consistent with law and appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow legal limits on authority and account for funding constraints when implementing the order's requirements.
